summary: AgniWatch is an AI-powered satellite intelligence platform designed to make wildfire observation data easier to explore and understand. The platform brings together NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations in a unified dashboard, enabling users to visualize geographic fire activity, compare satellite sensors, explore temporal patterns, and review observation timestamps in UTC. It includes an interactive dashboard, fire map, sensor comparison, activity calendar, analytics, and transparent data-source information. AgniWatch uses satellite observation records to support environmental awareness, research, and data exploration. The project combines a web-based interface with structured data processing and storage. Its publicly accessible demonstration currently presents a curated sample of genuine NASA MODIS and VIIRS observations rather than a continuous live satellite feed or the complete indexed database. AgniWatch aims to make satellite-derived fire intelligence more accessible to students, researchers, and environmental stakeholders.
details:
AgniWatch is a satellite fire intelligence platform developed by Team ORBIT X for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its objective is to transform satellite-based active-fire observations into an accessible and interactive visual experience.

The platform integrates observation records from two complementary NASA satellite systems: MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), aboard Terra and Aqua, and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite), aboard Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20. These sensors provide different observation characteristics, allowing users to explore and compare their fire detection records.

AgniWatch provides a centralized dashboard with the following capabilities:

• Interactive Dashboard: Displays an overview of fire observation activity and key information.
• Geographic Fire Map: Enables users to explore observation locations using geographic coordinates.
• Sensor Comparison: Provides a comparative view of MODIS and VIIRS observations.
• Activity Calendar: Supports exploration of observation activity across dates.
• Analytics: Presents visual summaries of satellite observation patterns.
• Data Sources and Methodology: Communicates the sensor references, spatial standards, temporal standards, and limitations of the data.

The frontend is developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. The backend architecture uses Python and FastAPI, with SQLite for structured data storage. The public frontend is deployed through Cloudflare Workers.

The platform follows consistent handling of source coordinates, sensor identification, and UTC acquisition timestamps to improve clarity and traceability. It is designed to support environmental awareness, educational exploration, and research-oriented analysis of satellite fire observations.

The current publicly accessible demonstration uses a curated sample of NASA MODIS and VIIRS observations. It is not a continuous live satellite feed and does not expose the complete indexed database. The platform's future scope includes automated data ingestion, verified near-real-time updates, AI-assisted fire-risk analysis, and alerting capabilities.

AgniWatch aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite observation records and an understandable interface for exploring wildfire activity.
